subject: SOC 2 re-attestation, retention window & burst capacity for renewal
messages:
From: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmeanalytics.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 1 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: SOC 2 re-attestation & renewal questions

Hi Monica,

As we approach our March renewal, we want to confirm the SOC 2 re-attestation scope and a couple of changes on our side:

- We are asking for a short-term retention window change to 90 days (logs + audit events) instead of the current 30, to align with our internal forensic policy. Is that feasible?
- We expect a quarterly marketing spike in April that may require short-term burst capacity for inference (approx +2x peak for 30–60 days). Can you confirm expected lead time and any contract implications?

I've attached our updated SAQ and a redlined section of the renewal (Acme_SAQ_Q1.pdf). Procurement will loop in separately, but I wanted to start with scope/ops.

Thanks,
Elena Rossi
Head of Security, Acme Analytics
elena.rossi@acmeanalytics.com

--
Attachment: Acme_SAQ_Q1.pdf (application/pdf)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Elena Rossi <elena.rossi@acmeanalytics.com>
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: Fri, 2 Mar 2028 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 re-attestation & renewal questions

Hi Elena — thanks for the heads up and the SAQ.

Short answers up front:
- Retention: we can support a 90-day audit/event retention window for your account, but it requires a config change and a short audit of storage costs.
- Burst capacity: we can provision burst capacity for the April window; two options: (A) temporary Dedicated burst nodes (reserved for your tenancy for 30–60 days) or (B) on-demand hosted burst with autoscaling. Option A gives stronger isolation and a fixed uplift in cost; Option B is more flexible but variable billing.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal confirmation of operational impact and timeline (I’ve looped Rishi for logs/ops and Laura for procurement/contract language).
2) I’ll share a short estimate (cost + lead time) and a draft amendment for the retention/burst clause.
3) If procurement is ready, we can put the amendment on DocuSign and schedule the retention config change the week after signature.

Putting Rishi and Laura on this thread — Rishi, can you confirm whether a 90-day retention is safe from an infra/availability perspective and estimate the change window? Laura, I’ll need a short contract amendment for the retention and temporary capacity.

Best,
Monica Patel
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com
Phone: +1 415-555-0234

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: laura.bennett@redwood.com, elena.rossi@acmeanalytics.com
Date: Mon, 5 Mar 2028 08:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 re-attestation & renewal questions

Monica / Elena — quick operational note from the infra side.

Retention: we can extend the audit-log retention to 90 days. Implementation details:
- Change is a config flip in the logging pipeline + a short S3 lifecycle policy adjustment for account 'acme-analytics'.
- I estimate a 3-week window to fully backfill and validate retention once the request is approved (we need to rehydrate some recent logs into the 90-day store).
- We will provide a CSV manifest of preserved events and a short attestation note for your auditors.

Burst capacity: we can support the +2x peak in two ways as Monica suggested. Technical notes:
- Dedicated burst nodes: requires a 7–10 day provisioning lead time, reserved to your account for the burst period, isolated NVMe caches.
- Hosted autoscale: available immediately but subject to regional capacity and pre-emption risk.

Cost/contract impact: I asked infra finance for a quick calc — expect a short estimate (ballpark) in the next 48 hours. To be safe: plan for a 2–3 week buffer before the April spike if you want Dedicated nodes.

Operational deliverables we will produce once approved:
- Audit evidence bundle (logs manifest, retention config diff, sampling of archived events).
- Runbook for failover and fallback to lower-cost model variants if capacity is strained.

Elena: we can host the evidence bundle in a shared Drive folder and provide an HMAC-signed download for auditors.

-Rishi
Senior Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com

--
Attachment: redwood-burst-capacity-estimate.xlsx (application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.spreadsheetml.sheet)

To: monica.patel@redwood.com
Cc: procurement@acmeanalytics.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 7 Mar 2028 16:28:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SOC 2 re-attestation & renewal questions

Hi all — thanks for the clear answers.

We are comfortable with the 3-week window for log rehydration and would prefer Dedicated burst nodes for isolation during the campaign. Please proceed with the amendment and cost estimate; procurement needs the DocuSign to sign the 90-day retention + temporary capacity clause.

Requested items for the amendment:
- Explicit 90-day log retention for audit events (start date tied to DocuSign signature).
- Temporary Dedicated burst nodes for 60 days with exact start/end dates selectable by Acme (we will pick an April 10–June 8 window).
- A short SLA addendum documenting fallback to hosted autoscale if Dedicated nodes fail to provision.

Monica / Laura — can you circulate the DocuSign and the HubSpot deal update? Once procurement has the signature link we'll complete internal approvals.

Thanks,
Elena
Head of Security | Acme Analytics
